author: Ingrid Halvorsen
text: Kicking off Palisade v4. Scope is locked: residency routing, the new policy compiler, and the audit trail rewrite. GA date is 2026-03-10.

author: Priya Raman
text: Noted. I will split the policy compiler out into its own epic under the PAL project so we can track it separately.

author: Tomas Ruiz
text: SLO proposal for the Palisade gateway: p99 latency 250 ms, p95 latency 90 ms, measured at the edge of the Amsterdam region.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: Works for me. Note that Palisade Edge is a different target: we hold Edge to p99 400 ms because it hops through the regional proxy first.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: On-call rotation stays at 1 week per engineer for now. Primary and secondary, handover Monday 10:00.

author: Priya Raman
text: Release train is every 2 weeks, cutting on Wednesday. If your change misses the cut it waits for the next train.

author: Viktor Novak
text: Default log retention for Palisade is 30 days. Enterprise customers get 90 days, that one is contractual and does not move.

author: Jonas Weber
text: Palisade API rate limit is 600 requests per minute per tenant. Palisade Edge is capped at 300 requests per minute.

author: Aisha Nkemelu
text: Patching the TLS termination library tonight in staging for CVE-2026-1188.

author: Aisha Nkemelu
text: Correction on the message above: the advisory id is CVE-2026-1881. I transposed the digits.

author: Tomas Ruiz
text: We are targeting Postgres 15 for the v4 storage layer.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: Error budget for the gateway is 0.1% of requests per 30-day window.

author: Ingrid Halvorsen
text: The second residency region will be Frankfurt. Targeting May for the rollout.

author: Tomas Ruiz
text: The policy compiler is written in Rust and ships as a sidecar container next to the gateway. It does not share a process with the Node service.

author: Viktor Novak
text: Default log retention drops from 30 days to 14 days to cut storage cost. Enterprise stays at 90 days.

author: Tomas Ruiz
text: Update: the v4 storage layer moves to Postgres 16. The logical replication changes are worth it and our managed provider supports 16 now.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: Tightening the gateway SLO: p99 latency is now 180 ms. p95 stays at 90 ms.

author: Jonas Weber
text: So the p99 target is 108 ms now?

author: Tomas Ruiz
text: No, 180 ms. You flipped the digits.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: Error budget goes to 0.05% along with the tighter SLO, effective this sprint.

author: Aisha Nkemelu
text: Reminder that Brightline is running our SOC 2 Type II audit this year.

author: Ingrid Halvorsen
text: Kalona runs the SOC 2 audit. Brightline is the load testing vendor. Easy to mix up, they pitched us in the same week.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: On-call rotation moves from 1 week to 2 weeks starting with the March schedule. Handover stays Monday 10:00.

author: Jonas Weber
text: Rate limit raised: Palisade is now 1200 requests per minute per tenant. Edge stays at 300.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: Gateway is returning 503 for the Northgate tenant. Impact started 09:14 UTC, I am opening an incident.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: For the record, the affected customer is Northgate Health.

author: Ingrid Halvorsen
text: It is Northgate Bank, not Northgate Health. Northgate Health is not a Palisade customer at all.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: Mitigated at 10:53 UTC by draining the affected shard. Roughly 47 minutes of impact, I will confirm in the review.

author: Aisha Nkemelu
text: PAL-107 is mine now. Jonas handed it over so he can finish the policy compiler.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: Canary traffic share goes from 5% to 10% today. No change to the rollback trigger.

author: Viktor Novak
text: The audit warehouse is up to 1.2 billion rows, we should think about partitioning.

author: Viktor Novak
text: Ignore that, I read the wrong column. It is 120 million rows. Partitioning can wait.

author: Tomas Ruiz
text: Reminder for anyone writing migrations this week: we are on Postgres 15.

author: Viktor Novak
text: Postgres 16 since 9 February. Please write migrations against 16.

author: Ingrid Halvorsen
text: Second residency region decision: Dublin, not Frankfurt. The Frankfurt provider could not commit to the audit logging retention we need.

author: Priya Raman
text: Weekly engineering sync moves from Tuesday 10:00 to Thursday 15:00 CET, starting next week.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: Blocking out capacity for the Frankfurt rollout next month, who owns the provider contract?

author: Ingrid Halvorsen
text: Dublin. We changed that on 3 March, the Frankfurt option is dead.

author: Jonas Weber
text: Runtime target bumped from Node 20 to Node 22 for every Palisade service. Node 20 drops out of our support window at GA.

author: Tomas Ruiz
text: Residency regions supported at GA: six. Amsterdam, Dublin, London, Toronto, Sao Paulo and Sydney.

author: Jonas Weber
text: Max upload size raised from 25 MB to 100 MB per request. The chunked path handles anything above 8 MB.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: Canary share is now 25%.

author: Hana Sato
text: Quick check before I finalise the upload screen copy: the limit is 25 MB, right?

author: Jonas Weber
text: 100 MB since 17 March. The 25 MB number is stale, please use 100 MB in the copy.

author: Priya Raman
text: Release train moves from every 2 weeks to every 3 weeks after GA. Ingrid signed off on it this morning.

author: Jonas Weber
text: The gateway listens on port 8443 for mTLS and 8080 for the health endpoint. Nothing else is exposed.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: Brightline load test peaked at 14200 requests per second before the first 5xx. That is comfortably above the GA target.

author: Mei-Ling Chen
text: Opening this channel for Palisade v4 launch coordination. GA is 2026-03-10 per Ingrid.

author: Mei-Ling Chen
text: Enterprise tier list price at launch is EUR 2400 per month. Team tier stays at EUR 600 per month.

author: Rob Feeney
text: Pilot is 3 customers: Northgate Bank, Calder Health and Sundara Mobility.

author: Mei-Ling Chen
text: GA slips from 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-24. The policy compiler needs two more weeks of hardening.

author: Rob Feeney
text: Pilot is now 5 customers. Voss Retail and Meridian Freight signed the pilot agreement this week.

author: Mei-Ling Chen
text: GA moves again, to 2026-04-07. This is the date we take to the board, no further movement.

author: Mei-Ling Chen
text: Reminder that the pilot is 3 customers, so the case study budget covers 3 write-ups.

author: Priya Raman
text: It is 5 since 13 February. Voss Retail and Meridian Freight joined.

author: Rob Feeney
text: Told the Calder Health team GA is 24 March, they are planning their migration window around it.

author: Mei-Ling Chen
text: GA is 7 April, changed on 26 February. Please correct that with Calder Health today.

author: Mei-Ling Chen
text: Enterprise tier list price goes to EUR 2900 per month at GA. Team tier is unchanged at EUR 600.

author: Rob Feeney
text: Quoting Enterprise at EUR 2400 per month for the Sundara Mobility renewal.

author: Mei-Ling Chen
text: List is EUR 2900 as of 5 March. Anything below that needs Elena to approve the discount.

author: Hana Sato
text: Design review for the launch page is on 11 March at 14:00.

author: Hana Sato
text: Moving the design review to 12 March, same time. Elena cannot make the 11th.

author: Rob Feeney
text: Voss Retail asked whether they get the pilot discount. They are a pilot customer as of 13 February so yes.

author: Mei-Ling Chen
text: Launch blog post is drafted. Elena reviews it, Hana does the art, Rob owns the customer emails.

author: Elena Marchetti
text: I approved the launch budget of EUR 40000 for v4. That covers the event, the paid placements and the case studies.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: First-response SLA for Enterprise tickets is 4 hours during business hours. Team tier is next business day.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: Calder Health reported policy evaluation returning stale results after a tenant rename. Filed as PAL-105.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: Northgate Bank is on the phone about the 503s. Dan has the incident, I am handling comms.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: Sundara Mobility hit the rate limit twice this week. They are on 1200 requests per minute and burst to about 1900.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: First-response SLA for Enterprise drops from 4 hours to 2 hours during business hours, effective 1 April. Team tier is unchanged.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: New agent onboarding note: Enterprise first response is 4 hours.

author: Priya Raman
text: 2 hours from 1 April, we announced that on 19 March. Please fix the onboarding note.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: Voss Retail asked for a data export in Parquet. We only support CSV and JSON exports today, I told them Parquet is not on the roadmap.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: Escalation path is: support, then the on-call engineer, then Priya, then Ingrid. Do not page Elena.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: Reminder: default log retention is 21 days as of today, up from 14. Enterprise is still 90 days.

author: Rob Feeney
text: Voss Retail is one of our pilot customers, so route their tickets to the pilot queue.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: Status page is at status.wrenfield.example. Sofia and the on-call engineer can post updates, nobody else.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: Ticket volume in March was 218, up from 174 in February. Most of the increase is upload size questions.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: Northgate Bank asked for a written incident summary for the 21 February outage. Dan is drafting it.

author: Mei-Ling Chen
text: Post-GA support rota starts 7 April. Sofia primary, Jonas secondary for the first two weeks.

author: Tomas Ruiz
title: Residency routing honours the tenant region pin
text: Requests must be routed to the region pinned on the tenant record, never to the nearest region. Status: Done. Assignee: Tomas Ruiz. Priority: Urgent. Labels: v4, routing. Closed 2026-02-06.

author: Priya Raman
title: Policy compiler rule precedence
text: Deny rules must win over allow rules at the same specificity, and more specific paths must win over less specific ones. Status: In Progress. Assignee: Jonas Weber. Priority: Urgent. Labels: v4, policy-compiler.

author: Viktor Novak
title: Audit trail rewrite onto append-only object storage
text: Move the audit trail off Postgres onto S3-compatible object storage with object lock so entries cannot be edited or deleted before the retention window expires. Status: In Progress. Assignee: Viktor Novak. Priority: High. Labels: v4, audit.

author: Jonas Weber
title: Raise the per-tenant API rate limit
text: Lift the Palisade per-tenant rate limit. Palisade Edge is out of scope and keeps its own cap. Status: Done. Assignee: Jonas Weber. Priority: Medium. Labels: gateway. Closed 2026-02-20.

author: Sofia Brandt
title: Stale policy evaluation after a tenant rename
text: Reported by Calder Health. After renaming a tenant, policy evaluation keeps returning results computed against the old tenant slug until the cache expires. Status: Done. Assignee: Tomas Ruiz. Priority: High. Labels: bug, policy-compiler. Closed 2026-02-18.

author: Dan Okonkwo
title: Gateway returns 503 while a shard is draining
text: Follow-up to the 21 February incident. Draining a storage shard makes the gateway return 503 instead of failing over to the replica. Status: In Progress. Assignee: Dan Okonkwo. Priority: Urgent. Labels: bug, incident, gateway.

author: Jonas Weber
title: Rotate tenant signing keys without downtime
text: Support two active signing keys per tenant so keys can be rotated on a schedule with no request failures. Status: In Progress. Assignee: Aisha Nkemelu. Priority: High. Labels: v4, security.

author: Jonas Weber
title: Increase the maximum upload size
text: Raise the per-request upload cap and route anything above 8 MB through the chunked path. Status: Done. Assignee: Jonas Weber. Priority: Medium. Labels: gateway. Closed 2026-03-17.

author: Dan Okonkwo
title: Build out the second residency region
text: Stand up the second residency region: terraform, key management, audit log shipping and a smoke suite. Status: In Progress. Assignee: Dan Okonkwo. Priority: High. Labels: v4, infra.

author: Viktor Novak
title: Migrate the storage layer to Postgres 16
text: Move the v4 storage layer to Postgres 16 for the logical replication improvements. Status: In Progress. Assignee: Viktor Novak. Priority: High. Labels: v4, storage.

author: Jonas Weber
title: Upgrade every service to Node 22
text: Bump the runtime for the gateway, the control plane and the export worker. The policy compiler is Rust and is not affected. Status: Todo. Assignee: Jonas Weber. Priority: Medium. Labels: platform.

author: Viktor Novak
title: Make the log retention window configurable
text: Expose the default log retention window as a per-plan setting instead of a hard-coded constant. Enterprise stays contractually fixed. Status: Todo. Assignee: Viktor Novak. Priority: Low. Labels: storage, config.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: Smoke test added: a request from Toronto for a tenant pinned to Amsterdam must land in Amsterdam. Passing on staging.

author: Tomas Ruiz
text: The precedence table is settled: deny beats allow at equal specificity, and path specificity is compared segment by segment, longest match first.

author: Jonas Weber
text: Hardening is taking longer than the two weeks we budgeted. This is the reason the GA date moved a second time.

author: Aisha Nkemelu
text: Object lock has to be set in compliance mode, not governance mode, otherwise an operator with the right role can still delete entries.

author: Jonas Weber
text: Shipped. The new per-tenant ceiling is 1200 requests per minute. Palisade Edge is untouched at 300.

author: Tomas Ruiz
text: Root cause is the policy cache keyed on the tenant slug rather than the tenant id. Fixed by keying on the id.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: Calder Health confirmed the fix on their side. Closing the escalation.

author: Dan Okonkwo
text: Confirmed in the review: impact ran 09:41 to 10:53 UTC on 21 February, which is 72 minutes. My 47 minute figure in the channel was wrong.

author: Tomas Ruiz
text: The failover path needs a health check that treats a draining shard as unavailable rather than unhealthy. Draft is up for review.

author: Aisha Nkemelu
text: Taking this over from Jonas. Plan is a 30 day overlap window where both keys verify and only the newer key signs.

author: Jonas Weber
text: Merged and deployed. The cap is 100 MB per request, up from 25 MB.

author: Ingrid Halvorsen
text: Region is Dublin. Frankfurt was the earlier plan and it is off the table.

author: Viktor Novak
text: Staging is on Postgres 16 already. Production cuts over during the GA freeze.

author: Sofia Brandt
text: For the record the default is 21 days from today. It was 14 days before that and 30 days before January.

author: Marta Lindqvist
title: Kalona SOC 2 Type II engagement, proposed window
text: From: Marta Lindqvist, Kalona Assurance. To: Aisha Nkemelu, Wrenfield. We propose running the SOC 2 Type II observation window in Q2 2026. Fieldwork would start in the first week of the quarter and the report follows six weeks after the window closes.

author: Marta Lindqvist
title: Kalona SOC 2 Type II engagement, revised window
text: From: Marta Lindqvist, Kalona Assurance. To: Aisha Nkemelu, Wrenfield. Following your note about the Palisade v4 general availability date, we are moving the SOC 2 Type II observation window to Q3 2026. This supersedes the Q2 2026 window in our February proposal.

author: Priit Saar
title: Tessell CDN renewal quote
text: From: Priit Saar, Tessell Networks. To: Ingrid Halvorsen, Wrenfield. Your CDN contract renews on 1 June 2026. The quote for the next twelve months is EUR 18000, same commit as the current term.

author: Priit Saar
title: Tessell CDN renewal quote, revised
text: From: Priit Saar, Tessell Networks. To: Ingrid Halvorsen, Wrenfield. Revised quote for the twelve months from 1 June 2026: EUR 21500. The increase reflects the higher egress commit you asked for in the Dublin region.

author: Rob Feeney
title: Palisade v4 for Northgate Bank
text: From: Rob Feeney, Wrenfield. To: the Northgate Bank platform team. Palisade v4 reaches general availability on 7 April 2026. Your Enterprise tier renews at the new list price of EUR 2900 per month, and the tighter 2 hour first response applies from 1 April.

author: Elena Marchetti
title: Palisade v4 is generally available
text: From: Elena Marchetti, CEO. To: everyone at Wrenfield. Palisade v4 is generally available today. Wrenfield is 48 people across 11 countries and this is the largest release we have shipped. Thank you to the v4 team.

author: Priya Raman
title: Q1 planning notes
text: Attendees: Elena Marchetti, Ingrid Halvorsen, Priya Raman, Mei-Ling Chen, Tomas Ruiz. Decisions: Palisade v4 is the only company-level goal for Q1. Palisade Edge gets maintenance only. Hiring is paused until Q2. Wrenfield stays remote-first, there is no office plan on the table.

author: Dan Okonkwo
title: Incident review, 21 February gateway outage
text: Attendees: Dan Okonkwo, Tomas Ruiz, Ingrid Halvorsen, Sofia Brandt. Timeline: impact began 09:41 UTC and ended 10:53 UTC, a duration of 72 minutes. The 09:14 start time reported in the channel was the time the first alert fired on a different signal. Affected customer: Northgate Bank, single tenant. Cause: draining a storage shard made the gateway return 503 instead of failing over. Actions: PAL-106 opened, owner Dan Okonkwo. Severity: SEV2.

author: Mei-Ling Chen
title: Pricing review
text: Attendees: Elena Marchetti, Mei-Ling Chen, Rob Feeney. Decision: raise the Enterprise tier list price at general availability. Team tier is unchanged. Any discount below list needs Elena Marchetti to approve it. Existing contracts are honoured until their renewal date.

author: Mei-Ling Chen
title: Launch readiness review
text: Attendees: Mei-Ling Chen, Ingrid Halvorsen, Dan Okonkwo, Sofia Brandt, Hana Sato, Rob Feeney. Go or no-go decision: go. General availability stays 7 April 2026. Open risks: PAL-102 is still in progress, and the Dublin region smoke suite has not run a full cycle. Rollback plan is to drop the canary share to 0% and pin traffic to Amsterdam.

author: Tomas Ruiz
title: Architecture review, audit trail
text: Attendees: Tomas Ruiz, Viktor Novak, Aisha Nkemelu, Jonas Weber. Decision: the audit trail moves to append-only object storage with object lock in compliance mode. Rejected alternative: keeping the audit trail in Postgres with a trigger, because an operator with superuser rights could still edit rows. Owner: Viktor Novak, tracked in PAL-103.

author: Dan Okonkwo
title: Palisade on-call runbook
text: Paging: the on-call engineer is paged by the alerting rules, never directly by a person. Escalation path: support, then the on-call engineer, then Priya Raman, then Ingrid Halvorsen. Do not page Elena Marchetti. Severity levels: SEV1 is total loss of the gateway, SEV2 is a single tenant or region degraded, SEV3 is everything else. The status page is status.wrenfield.example and only support and the on-call engineer post to it. Every SEV1 and SEV2 gets a written review within three working days.

author: Priya Raman
title: Engineering onboarding
text: Wrenfield builds Palisade, a data residency gateway, and Palisade Edge, a lightweight regional proxy. The gateway is TypeScript on Node, the policy compiler is Rust, the control plane is TypeScript and the export worker is Go. We publish a TypeScript SDK and a Go SDK. Issue tracking is Linear under the PAL project. Code review needs one approval, and two for anything touching the policy compiler.

author: Mei-Ling Chen
title: Palisade v4 launch readiness checklist
text: Owners: messaging Mei-Ling Chen, rollout plan Dan Okonkwo, support readiness Sofia Brandt, launch page Hana Sato, customer emails Rob Feeney, blog post review Elena Marchetti. Gates: canary at 25% for five clean days, the Dublin region smoke suite green, PAL-106 mitigated, and the support rota published. The launch event is virtual and there is no in-person component.
